newsitem.title: UK: Foreign & Colonial to back Northern in bid.
newsitem.headline: Foreign & Colonial to back Northern in bid.

text.p: Foreign & Colonial, which holds just over one percent of bid target Northern Electric, will reject CE Electric's 650 pence per share offer, David Manning, head of institutional fund management, said.
"We will be rejecting the offer," he told Reuters.
Manning said the offer from CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by U.S. group CalEnergy, was lower than previous offers for regional electricity companies (Recs) "on any comparative basis."
"It is manifestly a low bid," he added.
Northern Electric has argued that CE Electric's bid, which it raised from 630 pence on December 6, undervalued the company and has pressed for a higher valuation.
CE Electric has said its 650 pence offer is final and has drawn a deadline of December 20 for acceptances.
Manning said the offer would also set a precedent for future Rec bids, which look increasingly likely after the UK approved CE Electric's offer on Friday.
"It would establish a new low level...it is not only this one bid but the rattle-on effect on others," Manning said.
CE Electric has argued that its valuation compares favourably with previous bids for Recs and with a current agreed offer for East Midlands Electricity from U.S.-based Dominion Resources.
There are three other Recs left which are independent and not currently courted -- Southern, London and Yorkshire.
Manning said Foreign & Colonial "generally supports management," and suggested an agreed bid would be viewed more favourbaly.
